question: Why do terminal learning-rate cooldown shapes produce different language-model losses, and which scheduler and AdamW choices work best during that phase?

key_findings.claim: Cooldown shape materially changes final validation perplexity even when the pre-cooldown checkpoint, data volume, and training budget are shared.
key_findings.evidence: Linear, cosine, mirrored cosine, square, square-root, and lowered-linear schedules trace visibly different perplexity paths and finish at different values.

key_findings.claim: The authors interpret schedule choice through an empirical bias-variance trade-off over nine data permutations; square-root and lowered-linear 0.7 lie near the best trade-off for a single final model.
key_findings.evidence: Bias is defined relative to a longer-trained averaged reference and variance as the average-member loss gap to a weight-averaged model; a related shift-deviation recency analysis produces similar ordering.

key_findings.claim: When four cooled models are weight-averaged, high-variance schedules perform best, but one equal-data/equal-FLOP longer run still beats every average.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 9 compares the four-run soups against a 52.8k-step square-root run and separates the recipe for a single checkpoint from the recipe for a model soup.

key_findings.claim: AdamW state timescales can matter as much as cooldown shape: very large beta2 values improve perplexity in the tested sweep, whereas matching token half-life while increasing batch size degrades performance.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 10-11 show that changing beta values spans roughly the same performance range as changing schedule shape; the square-root schedule remains the lower envelope except at unreasonable state-update settings.

method.core_idea: Hold the WSD stable-stage endpoint fixed and vary only cooldown schedules, data permutations, batch sizes, and optimizer-state half-lives.
method.mechanism: Compare individual and weight-averaged endpoints, decompose excess validation loss relative to a longer reference into empirical bias and variance, audit recency effects, and visualize two-dimensional loss slices along global and local Adam directions.
assumptions: Weight averaging across runs is meaningful because the models share a pre-cooldown checkpoint.
The chosen longer square-root run is a suitable reference for the bias term.
Moderate-scale validation perplexity and local loss slices predict useful large-scale scheduler behavior.

techniques.role: Separates terminal annealing geometry from the preceding training trajectory.
Uses data-order replicates and weight averaging to decompose endpoint loss.
Scales AdamW beta values according to batch-token memory and tests that convention directly.

evaluations.setting: Moderate transformer pretraining from a common checkpoint with 33k-step cooldowns and nine data permutations.
evaluations.metric: Validation perplexity, empirical bias, variance, and recency shift/deviation.
evaluations.result: Square-root and lowered-linear 0.7 balance single-model bias/variance; high-variance shapes are preferable for soups.
evaluations.baseline: Linear, cosine, mirrored cosine, square, constant-start lowered-linear schedules, and a longer run.

evaluations.setting: Batch-size and AdamW beta sweeps during square-root cooldown.
evaluations.result: Beta selection produces differences comparable to schedule selection, with unusually high beta2 best in the observed sweep.
evaluations.baseline: Default beta1=0.9, beta2=0.95 and token-half-life-matched variants.

limitations: The main analysis is limited to moderate model sizes and validation loss, not downstream behavior.
The bias term depends on a particular longer-trained reference rather than an inaccessible optimum.
Two-dimensional loss-landscape slices are illustrative and do not establish global valley geometry.
The best beta2 may depend on model scale, data order, batch size, precision, and cooldown length.
failure_modes: A schedule tuned for a single endpoint may be suboptimal when endpoints are averaged.
Copying the reported beta2 to a different batch/scale can freeze the second-moment estimate or destabilize updates.
A short cooldown sweep can favor schedules whose advantages disappear with a longer horizon.
reusable_insights: The optimization target must say whether the deliverable is one model or an average of branches.
Optimizer-state time constants should be tuned with the schedule rather than treated as invariant defaults.
Shared-checkpoint branch experiments are a compute-efficient way to isolate terminal training choices.
open_questions: Do the schedule/beta rankings predict downstream capability and calibration?
Can bias and variance be estimated without choosing one long-run reference?
How do the optima scale with model size, cooldown fraction, and token batch size?

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Warmup-Stable-Decay Learning Rates: A River Valley Loss Landscape Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: The river-valley work motivates indefinite stable training and terminal descent; the target directly compares cooldown shapes, beta settings, and shared-checkpoint bias/variance.

competitive_landscape.title: MiniCPM: Unveiling the Potential of Small Language Models with Scalable Training Strategies
competitive_landscape.relationship: Prominent empirical use and scaling of WSD training.
competitive_landscape.difference: MiniCPM uses WSD as a scalable training recipe; the target isolates the cooldown and audits why its detailed shape and optimizer state matter.

competitive_landscape.title: The Surprising Agreement Between Convex Optimization Theory and Learning-Rate Scheduling for Large Model Training
competitive_landscape.relationship: Contemporary theoretical account of large-model schedule behavior.
competitive_landscape.difference: That work relates empirical schedules to convex-optimization bounds; the target supplies branch experiments, a bias-variance interpretation, and loss-landscape slices specific to WSD cooldowns.

novelty_assessment: The contribution is a careful cooldown-only empirical decomposition and the observation that AdamW memory tuning can rival schedule-shape tuning. WSD and the river-valley account predate it, and neither the empirical decomposition nor 2-D slices constitute a general theory of terminal annealing.
reviewer_notes: Read all 29 extracted pages, including replication datasets, weight-space alternatives, beta/batch appendices, and the paper's unresolved feature-probe section. Primary-source competitor pages were checked on 2026-08-23.
